chunk_1.page_content:
# 1 Introduction

This Interface Requirements Specification (IRS) defines five example packet formats used to exercise packet-definition extraction and validation. Each packet definition specifies its field layout, lengths, encoding, and validation requirements. Implementations shall follow the requirements stated for each packet type.

chunk_3.page_content:
## 2.1 Byte and Bit Numbering

Byte offsets are zero-based and are measured from the first byte of the packet. Within a byte, bit 0 is the least significant bit (LSB) and bit 7 is the most significant bit (MSB), unless a packet-specific requirement states otherwise.

chunk_4.page_content:
## 2.2 Numeric and Text Encoding

Multi-byte numeric fields use the byte order specified in the applicable packet definition. ASCII fields contain ASCII characters. UTF-8 fields contain valid UTF-8 encoded text. A field's declared byte length refers to its encoded byte length, not its character count.

chunk_5.page_content:
## 2.3 Field Ordering and Lengths

Fields appear in the order listed in each packet's field-layout table. Fixed-size fields occupy the stated number of bytes. Variable-size fields derive their length from the associated length field, count field, or packet-specific rule.

chunk_6.page_content:
## 2.4 Reserved Values and Validation

Reserved bits and fields shall be transmitted as zero unless otherwise stated. Receivers shall validate fixed values, enumerations, ranges, lengths, and checksums where specified. A packet that violates a mandatory validation requirement shall be rejected.

chunk_9.page_content:
### 3.1.1 Packet Overview

The Sample Packet is a fixed-length packet of 34 bytes. It contains a six-byte header, a fixed-width name, two one-byte numeric fields, and a six-byte footer.

chunk_10.page_content:
### 3.1.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Header 6 ASCII Must contain the exact value SAMPLE.
Name 20 ASCII Name text followed by NULL (0x00) padding to exactly 20 bytes.
Age 1 Unsigned 8-bit integer Valid range: 0–120.
Roll Number 1 Unsigned 8-bit integer Valid range: 1–255.
Footer 6 ASCII Must contain the exact value END123.

chunk_11.page_content:
### 3.1.3 Packet Length Validation

The packet shall be exactly 34 bytes long. The Header shall occupy bytes 0–5, Name bytes 6–25, Age byte 26, Roll Number byte 27, and Footer bytes 28–33. The receiver shall reject packets with an incorrect total length, header, footer, or field value outside the stated range.

chunk_13.page_content:
### 3.2.1 Packet Overview

The Status Flags Packet is a fixed-length packet of 8 bytes. It carries control flags, a status enumeration, a counter, and an event identifier.

chunk_14.page_content:
### 3.2.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Control 1 Bit field Bit 0: Enabled; bit 1: Alarm; bits 2–7: reserved and shall be zero.
Status 1 Unsigned 8-bit enumeration 0 = Idle; 1 = Active; 2 = Warning; 3 = Error. Other values are invalid.
Counter 2 Unsigned 16-bit integer, little-endian Valid range: 0–65535.
Event ID 4 Unsigned 32-bit integer, little-endian Valid range: 0–4294967295.

chunk_15.page_content:
### 3.2.3 Bit and Value Validation

The packet shall be exactly 8 bytes. Reserved Control bits shall be zero. Status shall be one of the defined enumeration values. Counter and Event ID shall be decoded as little-endian unsigned integers.

chunk_17.page_content:
### 3.3.1 Packet Overview

The Conditional Metadata Packet contains a control byte, optional metadata, a payload length, a variable-length payload, and a sequence number. The metadata field is present only when the Include Metadata flag is set.

chunk_18.page_content:
### 3.3.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Flags 1 Bit field Bit 0: Include Metadata (0 = absent, 1 = present); bits 1–7 reserved and zero.
Metadata 4 Unsigned 32-bit integer, little-endian Present only when Include Metadata = 1.
Payload Length 1 Unsigned 8-bit integer Number of bytes in Payload; valid range 0–255.
Payload Payload Length Byte array May contain zero bytes; its length shall equal Payload Length.
Sequence Number 2 Unsigned 16-bit integer, little-endian Present after Payload.

chunk_19.page_content:
### 3.3.3 Conditional Presence and Length Validation

The minimum packet length is 4 bytes when Metadata is absent and Payload Length is zero. When Metadata is present, the packet includes the additional 4-byte Metadata field. Total packet length shall equal 1 + (4 if Include Metadata = 1 else 0) + 1 + Payload Length + 2 bytes. The receiver shall reject reserved flag bits, truncated fields, or trailing bytes beyond the computed packet length.

chunk_21.page_content:
### 3.4.1 Packet Overview

The Text Command Packet carries a length-prefixed UTF-8 command string, a signed numeric parameter, and a CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE checksum.

chunk_22.page_content:
### 3.4.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Text Length 2 Unsigned 16-bit integer, big-endian Number of encoded bytes in Command Text.
Command Text Text Length UTF-8 byte sequence Must be valid UTF-8. A zero-length command is permitted unless disallowed by the application.
Parameter 4 Signed 32-bit integer, little-endian Valid range: -2147483648 to 2147483647.
Checksum 2 Unsigned 16-bit integer, big-endian CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over all preceding packet bytes; polynomial 0x1021, initial value 0xFFFF, no reflection, xor-out 0x0000.

chunk_23.page_content:
### 3.4.3 Text, Range, and Checksum Validation

The packet shall contain exactly 2 + Text Length + 4 + 2 bytes. Text Length counts UTF-8 encoded bytes, not Unicode characters. The receiver shall reject invalid UTF-8, truncated or excess data, and a checksum that does not match the CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE calculation over the bytes preceding the Checksum field.

chunk_25.page_content:
### 3.5.1 Packet Overview

The Sensor Batch Packet contains a record count followed by zero or more fixed-size sensor records. Each record reports a sensor identifier, signed reading, and quality code.

chunk_26.page_content:
### 3.5.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Record Count 1 Unsigned 8-bit integer Number of Sensor Records; valid range 0–255.
Sensor Records Record Count × 5 Repeated record structure Exactly Record Count records follow.
Sensor ID (per record) 2 Unsigned 16-bit integer, little-endian Valid range: 0–65535.
Reading (per record) 2 Signed 16-bit integer, little-endian Valid range: -32768 to 32767.
Quality (per record) 1 Unsigned 8-bit enumeration 0 = Unknown; 1 = Good; 2 = Degraded; 3 = Fault. Other values are invalid.

chunk_27.page_content:
### 3.5.3 Repeated Record and Value Validation

The packet length shall equal 1 + (Record Count × 5) bytes. A Record Count of zero is valid and produces a one-byte packet containing only Record Count. The receiver shall reject packets whose length does not match the declared record count or whose Quality value is not defined.

chunk_29.page_content:
## 4.1 Fixed-Length Packets

The Sample Packet shall be 34 bytes. The Status Flags Packet shall be 8 bytes. Both require exact-length validation.

chunk_30.page_content:
## 4.2 Conditional and Variable-Length Packets

The Conditional Metadata Packet length depends on the Include Metadata flag and Payload Length. The Text Command Packet length depends on Text Length and includes a two-byte checksum.

chunk_31.page_content:
## 4.3 Repeated-Record Packet

The Sensor Batch Packet length depends on Record Count. Each record is exactly 5 bytes, and zero records are permitted.

chunk_32.page_content:
# 5 Document Notes

This IRS is an illustrative test specification. Where a receiver encounters a malformed packet, it shall reject the packet rather than silently infer missing fields or repair inconsistent lengths. Packet-specific requirements in Section 3 take precedence over general conventions only where an explicit exception is stated.
